title: Vertebral fracture and amputation
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's vertebral fracture or amputation (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for L1 compression fracture.

HPI
Pt is an 80 y.o. female presenting for 8-week f/u following a traumatic closed wedge compression fracture of the L1 vertebra sustained from a ladder fall. Pt reports significant improvement in back pain since initial injury. She describes the site as stable and reports no new neurologic deficits. She is currently engaging in light activity and reports that the fracture is healing as expected. No new complaints of radicular pain or weakness.

Medication List
- Paracetamol 500mg BID PRN for pain
- Multivitamin daily

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, weight loss.
Musculoskeletal: Reports mild, dull aching in lower back, but no sharp pain. No joint swelling.
Neurologic: Denies numbness, tingling, or weakness in extremities.
Respiratory: Denies SOB or cough.
CV: Denies chest pain or palpitations.

Social History
Retired. Lives in a single-story home with her spouse. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension. Father: Heart disease.

Vitals
BP: 128/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Ht: 12.4
WBC: 7.2
HbA1c: 5.8%
eGFR: 74

Exam
General: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
Back: Stable, well-aligned, no midline step-off. No erythema or fluctuance.
Neuro: Motor strength 5/5 throughout. Sensation intact to light touch. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric.
Musculoskeletal: Normal range of motion of the spine.

Assessment
1. Traumatic compression fracture of the first lumbar vertebra (L1). Pt is progressing well; the site shows evidence of routine healing.
2. Normal bone density.

Plan
1. Continue current activity level. Avoid heavy lifting or strenuous twisting.
2. Follow up in 4 weeks for reassessment of progress.
3. Continue analgesics as needed for discomfort.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Routine follow-up while the L1 fracture heals: 7th character D, S32.010D (no HCC).
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: S32, M80, S88, Z89

distractors.why: Active treatment is complete; this is routine healing follow-up.
